$comment: Workflows available to every feature. A project can add or override entries in <project>/.claude/workbench-workflows.json (same shape, matched by id). kind 'prompt' sends the template to the feature's Claude session; kind 'script' runs the command in the project folder and shows the output. Templates can use {{feature.title}}, {{feature.id}}, {{feature.description}}, {{remote.url}}.

workflows.name: Plan it
workflows.description: Read the code and propose a step-by-step plan before changing anything.
workflows.template: Before changing anything, read the relevant code and propose a step-by-step plan for "{{feature.title}}". List the files you would touch, the risks, and how we'll know it works. Ask me anything you need decided.

workflows.name: Review changes
workflows.description: Review the uncommitted changes for bugs, then summarize them.
workflows.template: Review the uncommitted changes in this project for "{{feature.title}}". Look for correctness bugs first, then anything confusing or untested. Report findings most severe first with file:line. Don't fix anything yet.

workflows.name: Write tests
workflows.description: Add or extend tests covering this feature's behavior and run them.
workflows.template: Write tests that cover the behavior added for "{{feature.title}}". Follow the project's existing test setup; if there is none, propose the lightest one and ask before adding dependencies. Run them and report the results.

workflows.name: Draft PR description
workflows.description: Summarize the work so far as a pull request description.
workflows.template: Draft a pull request description for "{{feature.title}}" from the changes so far: what changed, why, how it was tested, and anything reviewers should look at closely. Link {{remote.url}} if it is set. Output Markdown only; don't create the PR.

workflows.name: Git status
workflows.description: Show the working tree status and the last few commits.

workflows.name: Run tests
workflows.description: Run npm test if the project defines one.
workflows.command: if [ -f package.json ]; then npm test --if-present 2>&1; else echo 'No package.json in this project.'; fi
